quickStart.title: Quick Start (2 minutes, no API key)
quickStart.step1: Install the extension and open Gmail.
quickStart.step2: Sign in to your Odoo in the same Chrome browser — the extension uses your active session.
quickStart.step3: Enter your Odoo URL (e.g. https://yourcompany.odoo.com — HTTPS, no trailing slash) and click Connect to Odoo. On odoo.com you can also click Autodetect Odoo to find it in an open tab.
quickStart.outro: Open any email and your Odoo contact appears in the sidebar. That's it — no API key, no code.

installation.title: Installation
installation.odooVersion: Version 14.0 or higher (on-premise, Odoo.sh, or Odoo Online Custom plan)
installation.step1Desc: Go to Odoo Integration for Gmail or search for "Odoo Integration for Gmail" in Chrome Web Store.
installation.step2Desc: Click the "Add to Chrome" button and review the permissions requested.
installation.step3Desc: You'll see a confirmation message and the extension icon will appear in your Chrome toolbar.
installation.step4Desc: Click the puzzle icon in Chrome toolbar, find "Odoo Integration for Gmail", and click the pin icon.
installation.noteDesc: If you see a message saying "This extension is not trusted by Enhanced Safe Browsing", this is normal for newly published extensions. The extension has been reviewed and approved by Chrome Web Store.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.step1Desc: Navigate to mail.google.com and open any email to view the sidebar.
configuration.step2Desc: Make sure you're logged in to your Odoo instance in the same browser — the extension connects using your active session.
configuration.step3Desc: Enter your Odoo instance URL (e.g., https://yourcompany.odoo.com). Use HTTPS and don't include a trailing slash.
configuration.step4Desc: Click Connect to Odoo and the extension checks your active session. An API key is optional — automatic logging needs one, and it also works as a backup if your session expires.
configuration.updateDesc: To connect the extension to a different Odoo:
configuration.updateStep1: Click the menu button (three vertical dots ⋮) in the panel header and choose Settings
configuration.updateStep2: Open Connection and click Change Odoo
configuration.updateStep3: Enter the new address and connect
configuration.versionNote: Adding an API key is optional. If you add one, the steps to create it vary between Odoo versions.
configuration.versionNoteLink: See the detailed guide for your version →
configuration.updateApiKeyNote: To add or change your API key later, open Settings → Connection. Log out is there too, at the bottom of the section.
configuration.autoOpenDesc: By default the Odoo panel opens on its own every time you open an email. To open it only when you need it, turn off “Open the panel when you open an email” in Settings → General. The panel then stays closed until you click the Odoo icon in Gmail's right sidebar. The change applies immediately, with no need to reload Gmail.

free.contactViewingDesc: View Odoo partner information directly in Gmail
free.emailLoggingDesc: Log emails to Odoo with attachments
free.recordCreationDesc: Create leads, partners, tasks, and tickets

plus.tabsDesc: Switch between contact and company information
plus.relatedContactsDesc: Find colleagues from the same company
plus.settingsDesc: Choose which sections appear in the sidebar: Opportunities, Tasks, Tickets, Quotations, Sales orders, Company information, Related contacts, Messages in Odoo and Financial information
plus.quoteLevelsDesc: Control how much conversation history to include when logging
plus.groupingDesc: Group opportunities, tasks, and tickets by stage or status
plus.emailParticipantsDesc: View Odoo contact information for all email participants
plus.recentActivitiesDesc: See recent messages from Odoo's conversations for each contact
plus.notificationsDesc: Spot Odoo notification emails in your inbox with a label for each module, see where you were mentioned, and open them all from one shortcut
plus.autologDesc: Link a Gmail thread to one or more Odoo records and have every new email logged automatically into their chatter (currently in private beta)
plus.multiCompanyDesc: Switch between the companies you have access to in Odoo, with cross-company contact lookup when an email matches a partner that lives in a different company
plus.quotationsDesc: See the contact's draft and sent quotations in the sidebar, with the amount and how long each one has been waiting for an answer
plus.salesOrdersDesc: See the sales orders already confirmed for the contact, with the reference, total and date, and log emails about delivery or invoicing to the right order

emailLogging.title: Email Logging
emailLogging.step1: Open the email you want to log
emailLogging.step2: View the contact in the sidebar
emailLogging.step3: To log it on the contact, click Log email under their name
emailLogging.step4: To log it on an opportunity, task, ticket, quotation or sales order, click the envelope icon on its row
emailLogging.step5: A notice confirms where it was logged, with Undo in case you picked the wrong record. The envelope then shows a check mark
emailLogging.internalNoteDesc: Emails are logged as internal notes in Odoo's chatter. This means only internal users (employees) can see them. Portal users (customers) will NOT see logged emails. Notifications are only sent to internal followers of the record.
emailLogging.duplicateIntro: The extension has two layers of duplicate detection:
emailLogging.visualIndicatorDesc: Helps you identify at a glance which records already have this email
emailLogging.serverSideDesc: Odoo prevents duplicates even if the visual indicator has expired
emailLogging.importantDesc: Even without the visual indicator, you cannot accidentally create duplicates. Odoo's server validates every logging request and rejects duplicates.

recordMenu.title: Actions on a record
recordMenu.intro: Every opportunity, task, ticket, quotation, sales order and related contact has its own actions menu. Move the pointer over the row and click the ⋮ button that appears on its right edge. The menu always starts with Open in Odoo and Copy link.
recordMenu.copyLinkTitle: Copy a link to the record
recordMenu.copyLinkDesc: Copies a direct link to that record in Odoo, ready to paste into a reply or a chat. It points to the same record the row opens when you click it.
recordMenu.autoLogTitle: Turn automatic logging on or off
recordMenu.autoLogDesc: Turn on automatic logging links the current thread to that record; Turn off automatic logging unlinks it. The option only appears when automatic logging is available for the thread. While it is paused, it is shown but disabled, so you can tell a paused link from one that was never set up.
recordMenu.closingDesc: Options that don't apply to a row are left out rather than greyed out, so the menu only ever shows what you can actually do. Click anywhere outside it, or press Escape, to close it without triggering anything.

autolog.title: Automatic logging
autolog.intro: Automatic logging links a Gmail thread to one or more Odoo records so that every new email in that thread is logged into the record's chatter on its own — no need to click the envelope icon for each reply.
autolog.betaDesc: Automatic logging is currently in private beta. It will be available to all PLUS subscribers soon. To request early access, write to us from Send feedback in the panel's menu.
autolog.requirement1: PLUS plan (and beta access during the private beta)
autolog.requirement2: An API key, added in Settings → Connection. Automatic logging works in the background, even with Gmail closed, so it can't use your browser session
autolog.requirement3: The “Turn on automatic logging” switch on, in Settings → Email logging
autolog.activateTitle: How to Turn On Automatic Logging in a Thread
autolog.activateStep1: Open the email thread in Gmail and view the contact in the sidebar
autolog.activateStep2: Find the record you want to follow (an opportunity, task, ticket, sales order, or the contact itself)
autolog.activateStep3: For a record in one of the lists, open its ⋮ menu and choose Turn on automatic logging. For the contact itself, use the automatic logging button next to Log email. A notice confirms it, and a sync icon stays next to the record's name while automatic logging is on
autolog.activateStep4: From now on, every new email in this thread is logged automatically into the chatter of that record
autolog.forwardOnlyDesc: Automatic logging only looks forward. Emails that were already in the thread before you turned it on are NOT logged retroactively. To log older emails, use the envelope button as usual.
autolog.whatGetsLoggedDesc: Each new email is added as an internal note in the record's chatter, with:
autolog.logged1: A Gmail-style header (From, To, Date, Subject)
autolog.logged2: The email body without quoted history
autolog.logged3: The original date of the email (not the time it was processed)
autolog.logged4: Linked partners — recipients are matched in Odoo by email and attached to the message
autolog.logged5: An "Auto-logged from Gmail" footer linking back to the extension
autolog.internalNoteDesc: Emails logged automatically are saved as internal notes (mt_note), not public messages. Only internal Odoo users can see them — portal users (customers) won't.
autolog.multipleTitle: Linking a Thread to Several Records
autolog.multipleDesc: You can turn on automatic logging for the same thread on several records (for example, an opportunity and a task about the same conversation):
autolog.multiple2: 1 thread → several records: every new email is logged on each linked record, one after another.
autolog.multiple3: The same record cannot be linked twice from the same thread — duplicates are rejected.
autolog.fromSidebarDesc: When the open thread has automatic logging on for any record, an “Automatic logging” section, with the number of linked records, appears at the top of the sidebar:
autolog.fromSidebar1: Click the section to expand it and see every record linked to the current thread
autolog.fromSidebar2: Click on a record's name to open it in Odoo
autolog.fromSidebar3: Click the ✕ button to turn off automatic logging for that specific record
autolog.fromSettingsDesc: Open Settings → Email logging to manage every thread with automatic logging:
autolog.fromSettings1: Turn automatic logging on or off for all threads with a single switch
autolog.fromSettings3: See the threads with automatic logging, how many there are, and when it last checked
autolog.fromSettings4: Turn them all off at once with “Deactivate all”
autolog.limit1Desc: Only emails that arrive after you turn it on are logged. Existing emails must be logged by hand.
autolog.limit2Desc: A link with no new email for 90 days is removed automatically. Turn it on again to resume.
autolog.limit3Desc: If the linked record is deleted in Odoo, the link is removed automatically the next time the extension tries to log into it.
autolog.limit4Desc: If the Gmail connection expires or is revoked, automatic logging stops for all threads until you reconnect from Settings → Email logging.
autolog.requirement4: Gmail connected: click Connect Gmail in Settings → Email logging

relatedContacts.title: Working with related contacts
relatedContacts.intro: The Related Contacts section in the sidebar lists colleagues from the same company as the email's sender. From there, or from each contact's ⋮ menu, you can take quick actions on each contact without leaving Gmail.
relatedContacts.openInOdooDesc: Click anywhere on the contact card — the avatar, the name, or the job title — to open that contact's record in Odoo in a new tab.
relatedContacts.composeTitle: Send a new email to a contact
relatedContacts.composeDesc: Click the email icon next to a contact's address. If you don't have any draft open, Gmail opens a new compose window with that address pre-filled in the To field.
relatedContacts.addRecipientTitle: Add a contact to an email you're already writing
relatedContacts.addRecipientDesc: If a Gmail compose window is already open when you click the email icon, the contact is added as a recipient of that draft instead of opening a new one. The extension chooses where: if the To field is empty, the contact goes there; if it already has someone, the contact is added to CC and the compose minimises so you can keep clicking other contacts to build the recipient list.
relatedContacts.copyTitle: Copy a contact's email or phone
relatedContacts.copyDesc: Click the email or phone text — not the icon next to it — to copy it to your clipboard. A small toast confirms the copy.
relatedContacts.callDesc: Click the phone icon to start a call. The action is handed off to whichever app your system has registered for phone numbers — your mobile dialer, FaceTime, Skype, Microsoft Teams, etc. If no app is configured, the click does nothing.

recentActivities.title: Navigating messages in Odoo
recentActivities.intro: The Messages in Odoo section shows the latest Odoo emails and notes the contact appears in — on their record or on an opportunity, task, order… — so you can see what has been said without leaving Gmail.
recentActivities.timestampTitle: See exactly when a message was sent
recentActivities.timestampDesc: Each entry shows a relative date like "5 days ago". Hover the date to see the exact day and time, formatted in your browser's locale.
recentActivities.jumpTitle: Jump to a specific message in Odoo
recentActivities.jumpDesc: Click any entry in Messages in Odoo to open the related Odoo record in a new tab. On Odoo 18 and later, the click goes one step further: Odoo scrolls to that exact message and highlights it for you. On Odoo 16 and 17 the record opens normally — the click still saves you the navigation, you just have to scroll to find the message yourself.

opportunities.title: Managing Opportunities
opportunities.leadRecords1: Opportunities linked to the contact (by partner_id)
opportunities.creatingLeadsIntro: Convert an email conversation into an Odoo opportunity with one click:
opportunities.step1: Open the email you want to convert into a lead
opportunities.step2: View the contact in the sidebar
opportunities.happens1: The lead is created with the email subject as name
opportunities.happens2: Email body content is added as description
opportunities.happens3: The contact from the sidebar is linked
opportunities.happens4: The lead opens in Odoo in a new tab for additional editing
opportunities.happens5: While the record is being created the button shows a processing state, and repeated clicks won't create duplicates
opportunities.importantDesc: The email is NOT logged automatically. To associate the email with the new lead, return to Gmail and click the envelope icon next to the opportunity.

quotations.title: Pending quotations
quotations.intro: The Quotations section lists the contact's quotations that are still open — drafts and quotations already sent — so you can see what is waiting on a decision without leaving Gmail.
quotations.requirement1: PLUS plan. On the FREE plan the section is still there, locked, with a link to upgrade.
quotations.requirement2: Odoo Sales installed, and permission to create quotations. If your user has Sales in read-only mode, the section doesn't appear.
quotations.groupDraftDesc: quotations still in draft — the next move is yours.
quotations.groupSentDesc: already sent — the next move is the customer's.
quotations.timing: Each row shows the amount and a time signal: how long the quotation has been waiting ("Created 5 days ago"), or how soon it expires ("Expires tomorrow", "Expired"). Quotations that have expired, or expire within a week, are highlighted.
quotations.action1: Click a row to open the quotation in Odoo.
quotations.action2: Click the envelope icon to log the current email into that quotation's chatter.
quotations.action3: Click Create to start a new quotation for the contact and finish it in Odoo.
quotations.action4: Open the row's ⋮ menu to open the quotation in Odoo or copy a link to it, and use the search box when the list gets long.
quotations.continuityNote: When you confirm a quotation it leaves this list and moves to Confirmed sales orders, where you can keep logging the correspondence that follows.
quotations.hideNote: Don't work with quotations? Hide the section from Settings → Panel.

salesOrders.title: Confirmed sales orders
salesOrders.intro: The Sales Orders section lists the orders already confirmed for the contact, so the conversation that follows a sale — deliveries, changes in quantities, invoicing, issues — can be filed on the order itself.
salesOrders.continuity: It closes a real gap: once a quotation is confirmed it leaves the Quotations section, and until now no other section picked it up. From that point on an email could only be logged against the contact, right when correspondence is at its busiest.
salesOrders.requirement1: PLUS plan. On the FREE plan the section is still there, named, with a link to upgrade — and it makes no request to Odoo.
salesOrders.requirement2: Odoo Sales installed, and permission to read sales orders. Read access is enough: unlike Quotations, this section never creates records, so it also works for the profiles that follow orders without editing them.
salesOrders.list1: Live orders only: confirmed and in progress, locked ones included. Cancelled orders, and quotations not yet confirmed, stay out.
salesOrders.list2: Each row shows the order reference, its total with currency, and when it was placed. Most recent first.
salesOrders.list3: There is no age filter — an order counts as long as it is live, whatever its date. When there are more orders than fit, the header says how many are shown out of the total.
salesOrders.list4: On the company view the list also includes the orders of the contacts belonging to that company.
salesOrders.action1: Click a row to open the order in Odoo.
salesOrders.action2: Click the envelope icon to log the current email into that order's conversation. An order the email is already logged into is marked as such, and can't be logged twice.
salesOrders.action3: Open the row's ⋮ menu to copy a link to the order, or to turn on automatic logging so later emails in the thread are filed on the order without you doing anything.
salesOrders.action4: Use the search box to find an order by reference. It is the way to reach an older order that isn't among the most recent ones.
salesOrders.noCreateNote: The section doesn't create orders: an order comes from confirming a quotation in Odoo, not from reading an email.
salesOrders.hideNote: Don't follow up on orders from your inbox? Hide the section from Settings → Panel.

tasksTickets.title: Tasks & Tickets
tasksTickets.taskRecords1: Tasks linked to the contact (by partner_id)
tasksTickets.creatingTitle: Creating a Task or a Ticket from an Email
tasksTickets.creatingDesc: Click Create in the section. The record is created with the email subject and body, its attachments are uploaded in the background, and it opens in Odoo in a new tab so you can fill in the rest. While it's being created the button shows a processing state, and repeated clicks won't create duplicates.

financial.title: Financial insights
financial.intro: The Financial section sums up where the contact stands with you — what they owe, what you owe them, what is still to be invoiced — without opening Accounting in Odoo.
financial.companyNote: The figures belong to the company, not to the person: when the contact has a parent company in Odoo, the section shows that company's totals.
financial.requirement1: PLUS plan. On the FREE plan the section doesn't appear at all.
financial.requirement2: Odoo Invoicing or Accounting installed, and permission to read invoices. Without that permission the section stays hidden instead of showing an error.
financial.overdueDesc: the amount past due and how many invoices make it up. On Enterprise with Account Follow-up enabled, it also shows the next reminder date and the follow-up level. The block is there to inform: no action is attached to it.
financial.limitDesc: the limit set in Odoo, when there is one.
financial.invoicedDesc: the historical total for that company.
financial.dsoDesc: how many days invoices take to be paid, on average.
financial.emptyNote: A figure worth zero is left out instead of being shown as zero, so the section only lists what actually has a value. When nothing has a value and there is nothing overdue, the section stays out of the sidebar altogether — which is the normal case for a contact with no invoicing history.
financial.hideNote: Don't need the numbers in your inbox? Hide the section from Settings → Panel.

notifications.title: Odoo notifications
notifications.intro: Organize Odoo notification emails directly in your Gmail inbox. The extension recognizes notification emails from Odoo and labels them, so you can instantly see which module they belong to and whether you've been mentioned.
notifications.prerequisiteTitle: Prerequisite: Enable Email Notifications in Odoo
notifications.prerequisiteDesc: For this feature to work, your Odoo user must be configured to receive notifications by email (not in the Odoo inbox):
notifications.prerequisiteStep1: In Odoo, go to your Profile (top-right menu > My Profile)
notifications.prerequisiteStep3: Select "Handle by Emails" (instead of "Handle in Odoo")
notifications.prerequisiteNote: This ensures Odoo sends notification emails to your Gmail, where the extension can identify and organize them.
notifications.setupStep1Title: Find your notification email in Odoo
notifications.setupStep1Desc: Check a recent Odoo notification email in Gmail and look at the sender address (e.g., notifications@yourcompany.com). Alternatively, ask your Odoo administrator for the outgoing notification email.
notifications.setupStep2Desc: In the panel header, click the menu button (three vertical dots) and choose Settings.
notifications.setupStep3Desc: Open the Odoo notifications section, paste the address into Notification sender and click Save. The extension starts recognizing notification emails right away.
notifications.setupNoteDesc: If you're not sure which email Odoo uses for notifications, check a recent notification email in Gmail and look at the sender address.
notifications.moduleBadgesDesc: A label next to each notification email in your inbox shows which Odoo module sent it, and each module has its own color:
notifications.moduleBadge5: And more: Sales order, Purchase, Time off, Event, Mailing…
notifications.mentionBadgesDesc: When someone mentions you in an Odoo record (using @ or by name), a Mention label appears on the notification email:
notifications.mentionUnreadDesc: You have an unread mention — you haven't opened this email thread in Gmail since the mention
notifications.mentionReadDesc: You've already seen this mention — you opened the thread in Gmail after being mentioned
notifications.mentionHowItWorksDesc: Mention detection is based on the messages stored in the Odoo record, not the email itself. The extension checks the record's chatter for @mentions or references to your name. This means:
notifications.mentionHowItWorks1: If you recently switched from "Handle in Odoo" to "Handle by Emails", older threads may show a Mention label for mentions that happened before you started receiving emails — even though the mention won't appear in any Gmail email.
notifications.mentionHowItWorks2: The read/unread status is determined by whether you've opened the email thread in Gmail after being mentioned. Once you open the thread, the label turns gray.
notifications.shortcutDesc: An “Odoo notifications” shortcut appears in Gmail's left sidebar, below your labels. Click it to filter your inbox and show only Odoo notification emails.
notifications.shortcutNoteDesc: The shortcut only appears after you set the notification sender in Settings → Odoo notifications.
notifications.categoriesDesc: The “Odoo notifications” shortcut expands into sub-entries — Opportunities, Tasks, Tickets, Invoices and so on — each with its own unread count, so you can jump straight to the notifications of one module.
notifications.categoriesOther: Notifications coming from models outside that catalogue are grouped under a generic Odoo entry instead of being left out.
notifications.categoriesNote: Categories only appear for the modules you actually receive notifications from.
notifications.customizationDesc: Each part can be turned on or off in Settings → Odoo notifications:
notifications.customToggle1: Module label — show or hide the module labels
notifications.customToggle2: Mention label — show or hide the mention labels
notifications.customToggle3: Shortcut in the Gmail sidebar — show or hide “Odoo notifications” in Gmail's sidebar

multiCompany.title: Multi-Company Support
multiCompany.intro: If your Odoo user has access to several companies, the extension lets you choose which one is active. The active company decides which records the sidebar shows you and which company every new lead, task, ticket or contact is created in.
multiCompany.requirement2: An Odoo user with access to two or more companies (in Odoo: Settings > Users > Allowed Companies)
multiCompany.selectorDesc: When you have access to more than one company, a building icon appears in the panel header, next to the menu (⋮) button:
multiCompany.selector1: Hover the icon to see the active company name ("Operating in {company}")
multiCompany.selector2: Click the icon to open a menu with every company you have access to. The active one is highlighted
multiCompany.selector3: Pick a company. The menu closes and the sidebar refreshes with data from the new company
multiCompany.selector4: If you have access to only one company, the icon is not shown
multiCompany.persistDesc: Your selection is saved per Odoo instance, so opening Gmail again resumes the company you were last working in. Logging out clears the saved selection.
multiCompany.affectsDesc: Once you pick a company, every operation in the sidebar is scoped to it:
multiCompany.affects1Desc: Opportunities, tasks, tickets and partners listed in the sidebar are filtered to those visible in the active company
multiCompany.affects2Desc: New leads, tasks, tickets and contacts created from the sidebar are assigned to the active company
multiCompany.affects3Desc: Emails logged by automatic logging are posted in the company that owns the linked record (see Automatic Logging Across Companies below)
multiCompany.crossLookupIntro: If you open an email from someone who isn't in the active company but exists somewhere else in your Odoo instance, the sidebar tells you and offers actions instead of leaving you with an empty state.
multiCompany.crossContactTitle: The contact exists in another company
multiCompany.crossContactDesc: The sidebar shows the contact found, the company it lives in, and two actions:
multiCompany.crossContactAction1Desc: Removes the contact's company restriction so users in every company you have access to can see it. Asks for confirmation before saving
multiCompany.crossContactAction2Desc: Creates a separate contact record in the active company, leaving the original untouched
multiCompany.crossParentTitle: Only the parent company exists in another company
multiCompany.crossParentDesc: The contact is missing, but a related company (matched by email domain) exists in another of your companies. Two actions:
multiCompany.crossParentAction1Desc: Makes the parent company visible to every company you have access to, then lets you create the contact under it
multiCompany.crossParentAction2Desc: Creates an independent company record in the active company and the contact under it
multiCompany.shareWarningDesc: Sharing a contact or company across all your companies changes its visibility for every user with access to those companies. The extension asks for confirmation before saving.
multiCompany.autologDesc: When you turn on automatic logging for a record, the extension remembers the company that record belongs to. New emails on that thread are always logged in the right company, even if you've switched the active company in the sidebar afterwards.
multiCompany.freePlanDesc: If you have access to several companies on the FREE plan, the extension uses your default company in Odoo for every operation. The selector icon does not appear, and cross-company lookups are not offered. Upgrading to PLUS unlocks both.
multiCompany.limit1Label: Not synced with the Odoo browser switcher
multiCompany.limit1Desc: The extension keeps its own active company and sends it with every request, while the Odoo company switcher uses your browser session. The two are independent — switching companies in your Odoo tab does not change the active company in Gmail and vice versa.
multiCompany.limit2Desc: If your administrator changes your default company in Odoo, the extension keeps using the previously cached value until you log out and log back in.
multiCompany.limit3Desc: The selector is single-select: the sidebar shows records from one company at a time. To see records from another company, switch to it.
multiCompany.limit4Label: Access error after creating a record
multiCompany.limit4Desc: When you create an opportunity, task, ticket or contact from the sidebar (or click "View in Odoo" on one), the extension opens the record in a new browser tab. Odoo loads it under whichever company is currently active in your Odoo browser session (the cookie session — see above). If that company differs from the one where the record was created, Odoo may show an access error. On the FREE plan, the extension always creates records in your default Odoo company — to see them, switch your Odoo browser tab to that same default. On the PLUS plan, keep the same company selected in both the sidebar selector and your Odoo browser tab. Odoo 18 and later automatically switch your active company when you open a record that belongs to another of your allowed companies, so this issue is mostly visible on Odoo 17 and earlier.

troubleshooting.checkEnabledDesc: Go to chrome://extensions/ and ensure toggle is ON

troubleshooting.emailMismatchDesc: Capitalisation is not the problem: an address stored in Odoo as John@Acme.com does match john@acme.com. What breaks the match is a genuinely different address — an alias, an extra dot, or another domain. Update the email in Odoo, or create a new contact.
troubleshooting.sectionMissingIntro: Sections show up only when Odoo can serve them. If Opportunities, Tasks, Tickets, Quotations or Financial Insights is missing, check in this order:

troubleshooting.sidebarEmptyStep1Desc: Open your Odoo URL in another tab — if it asks you to log in, log in, then reload Gmail. The extension uses that session.
troubleshooting.sidebarEmptyStep2Desc: Use https://, your real instance URL, and no trailing slash. Self-hosted: use your custom domain.
troubleshooting.sidebarEmptyStep3: Open an actual email, not the inbox list
troubleshooting.sidebarEmptyStep3Desc: The contact card only loads inside an open email. Then reload Gmail (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R).
troubleshooting.sidebarEmptyOutro: Still stuck? Reply to your welcome email or send us a screenshot — we answer fast:
troubleshooting.sessionExpired: "Session Expired" or You're Asked to Reconnect
troubleshooting.sessionExpiredDesc: Your Odoo session timed out. Just open Odoo, sign in again, and the extension reconnects — nothing else to manage.
troubleshooting.sessionExpiredNote: An optional API key can be added as a backup so background features keep working when the session drops: Settings → Connection.
troubleshooting.selfHostedIntro: When connecting to a self-hosted Odoo instance (custom URL), Chrome requires additional permissions. If the permission popup doesn't appear:
troubleshooting.permissionPopupDesc: Custom Odoo URLs (not *.odoo.com) require an additional Chrome permission to communicate with your server
troubleshooting.extensionConflictDesc: Ad blockers, privacy extensions, or popup blockers can prevent Chrome's permission dialog from appearing
troubleshooting.temporaryDisableDesc: Temporarily disable other extensions (especially ad blockers) and try connecting again. Re-enable them after granting permission
troubleshooting.selfHostedNoteDesc: This permission is only required once per Odoo URL. After granting it, the extension will work normally with your self-hosted instance.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Q: What Odoo versions are supported?
faq.a1: Odoo 14.0 and higher are supported. Compatible with on-premise installations (Community/Enterprise), Odoo.sh, and Odoo Online (Custom plan only, as Standard and Free plans don't have external API access).
faq.q2: Q: Does it work with other browsers?
faq.a2: Currently, the extension only supports Google Chrome. Support for other browsers may be added in the future.
faq.qApiKey: Q: Do I need an API key?
faq.aApiKey: No. Just your Odoo URL and an active Odoo session in the same browser. An API key is optional — only for automatic logging (PLUS) or as a backup if your session expires.
faq.a3: Yes. The extension communicates with your Odoo instance over HTTPS, using your own Odoo session. It reads the emails you open and, only if you turn them on, the Odoo notifications and the threads you link for automatic logging. If you add an optional API key, it is stored in Chrome's storage; with Chrome sync on, Chrome also keeps it in your Google account.
faq.q4: Q: What's the difference between FREE and PLUS?
faq.a4: FREE includes contact viewing, email logging, record creation and the first 5 records of each section. PLUS adds every record with search and grouping, quotations and orders, Messages in Odoo, financial information, related contacts, Odoo notifications, several companies and customization.
faq.q5: Q: Can I cancel my PLUS subscription anytime?
faq.a5: Yes, you can cancel anytime without penalty. Your subscription will remain active until the end of your billing period.
faq.q6: Q: Does the extension read all my emails?
faq.a6: No. The extension reads the emails you open. With PLUS, two features work in the background, only if you turn them on: Odoo notifications (the emails your Odoo sends you) and automatic logging (the new emails in the threads you link). It never reads the content of the rest of your mailbox.
faq.q7: Q: Is my API key stored securely?
faq.a7: An API key is optional — most users connect with their Odoo session and never create one. If you do add one, it is stored in Chrome's storage (chrome.storage.sync): with Chrome sync on, Chrome copies it to your Google account and your other devices.
faq.q8: Q: What does the extension send when something goes wrong?
faq.a8: The error message and its technical details, the versions of the extension and of Odoo, and a random installation ID — never your email content or your credentials. If the error comes from your Odoo, it includes Odoo's error message, which may contain the address of your instance. These crash reports are sent even when usage analytics is turned off, because they describe the state of the app and not what you do with it. It is how a fault gets found and fixed without you having to report it. If you have or had PLUS, you can object at any time by writing to us from your license email; see the privacy policy for details.

overview.title: Overview
overview.intro: Odoo Integration for Gmail ("the Extension") is committed to protecting your privacy. This privacy policy explains how the Extension collects, uses, and protects your information.

infoCollect.title: Information We Collect
infoCollect.gmailDataDesc: The Extension accesses the following information from Gmail. Except where noted, only from the email you open:
infoCollect.senderRecipientDesc: Used to search for matching contacts in your Odoo instance
infoCollect.emailSubjectDesc: Used when you choose to create opportunities, tasks, or tickets in Odoo
infoCollect.emailDateDesc: Used for logging emails to Odoo records
infoCollect.odooDataDesc: The Extension retrieves the following information from your Odoo instance:
infoCollect.odooData1: Contact information (names, emails, phone numbers, companies)
infoCollect.autoLoggingDataDesc: Automatic logging is an opt-in feature. The Extension only accesses this data after you grant Gmail access in Settings > Email logging ("Connect Gmail") and explicitly link a thread to an Odoo record. Once a thread is linked, the Extension uses Google's Gmail API to:
infoCollect.autoLoggingData1: Periodically check the identifiers of the new messages in your account to find those in the threads you have linked (only while at least one thread is linked)
infoCollect.autoLoggingData2: Read the subject, sender, recipients, date and body of the new messages in those threads
infoCollect.autoLoggingData3: Post them as internal notes in the Odoo records you linked
infoCollect.autoLoggingDataNote: The Extension only requests the gmail.readonly OAuth scope. It cannot send, modify, archive or delete emails. Automatic logging stops when you turn it off for a thread or for all of them, or remove the Extension. Tokens can also be revoked from your Google Account permissions at any time.
infoCollect.configDataDesc: The Extension stores your configuration in Chrome's storage, in your browser:
infoCollect.configData5: Gmail OAuth tokens (only if you connect Gmail for automatic logging) — required to access the Gmail API on your behalf; they stay until you remove the Extension or revoke access from your Google Account
infoCollect.configData6: Automatic logging links (thread-to-record links and IDs of messages already logged) — stored in your browser while each link exists
infoCollect.configData7: Active company selection and the list of companies you have access to (multi-company instances) — cached locally to remember which company you are operating in
infoCollect.openTabsDesc: When you click "Autodetect Odoo", the extension reads the addresses of the odoo.com tabs open in this browser, only to offer you your instance. It does not read their content, and the addresses are neither stored nor sent.
infoCollect.notificationHeadersDesc: Only if you set up Odoo notifications: the Extension checks the sender of the emails in your Gmail lists and reads those your Odoo sends you, even if you don't open them, to label them by module
infoCollect.attachmentsDesc: Uploaded to your Odoo when you log an email or create a record from it
infoCollect.odooData6: Quotations, sales orders, financial figures and the messages the contact appears in
infoCollect.accountEmailDesc: Read when Gmail loads, to check that a PLUS license belongs to this account, and to fill it in when you subscribe

howWeUse.title: How We Use Your Information

howWeUse.displayContactDesc: Show relevant Odoo contact details in Gmail's sidebar

storage.localOnlyDesc: Configuration and cache are stored in Chrome's storage, in your browser. If you use Chrome sync, Chrome copies your Odoo address, your API key and your preferences to your Google account and your other devices.
storage.transmissionDesc: The Extension communicates directly with YOUR Odoo instance using HTTPS. Your Odoo credentials are never sent to the extension developer.

thirdParty.title: Third-Party Services
thirdParty.polarIntro: The Extension uses Polar (https://polar.sh/) for subscription management and payment processing. When you subscribe to the PLUS plan, Polar collects:

thirdParty.polar2: Payment information (processed securely by Stripe, not stored by the Extension)
thirdParty.importantDesc: Payment data is handled entirely by Polar and Stripe. The Extension never receives or stores your credit card information.
thirdParty.inboxsdkDesc: The Extension uses InboxSDK (https://www.inboxsdk.com/) to integrate with Gmail's interface: to display the sidebar and detect the contacts of the email you open.
thirdParty.posthogIntro: The Extension uses PostHog (https://posthog.com/) for usage analytics. PostHog helps us understand how the extension is used and identify issues. Data collected includes:
thirdParty.posthog1: Installation ID (a random code). If you activate PLUS, it is associated with your license.
thirdParty.posthog3: Error reports for debugging, without email content (see Crash reports below)
thirdParty.posthog4: A boolean flag indicating whether your Odoo user has access to more than one company (used to know whether multi-company features are relevant). The list of companies and their names are NOT sent.
thirdParty.optOutDesc: You can disable usage analytics at any time in Settings > General ("Share anonymous usage data"). That setting covers most usage statistics; crash reports (described below) and a few service events, such as a change of plan, are sent regardless.
thirdParty.errorReportsDesc: Crash reports are sent regardless of the analytics setting, because they describe the state of the application rather than your activity. Each report contains the error message and its technical details, the versions of the Extension and of Odoo, and the random installation ID — never email content or credentials. If the error comes from your Odoo, the report includes Odoo's error message, which may contain the address of your instance. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in detecting and fixing faults. If you have or had PLUS, you can object at any time by writing from your license email to
thirdParty.polar4: The installation ID, when you activate a license, to tell your devices apart
thirdParty.parityDesc: To show you the price for your country, the Extension asks ParityDeals (https://www.paritydeals.com/), which infers the country from your connection. It receives nothing from the Extension other than the request itself.

permissions.title: Permissions Explained
permissions.intro: The Extension requests the following Chrome permissions:
permissions.scripting: Required to inject the sidebar interface into Gmail
permissions.storage: Required to save your Odoo configuration and cache API responses in Chrome's storage
permissions.hostGmail: Required to access Gmail's interface and display the sidebar
permissions.hostOdoo: Required to communicate with Odoo Online cloud instances (e.g., yourcompany.odoo.com) and, when you click "Autodetect Odoo", to read the addresses of your open odoo.com tabs
permissions.hostPolar: Required for subscription management and payment processing
permissions.hostParity: Required to offer Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) discounts based on the user's country
permissions.optionalIntro: The Extension requests optional permissions for self-hosted Odoo instances and for automatic logging:
permissions.optionalDesc: Used ONLY if you connect to a self-hosted Odoo instance on a custom domain (e.g., odoo.yourcompany.com or erp.example.com), or for Google's API domain (www.googleapis.com) when you connect Gmail for automatic logging. Each address is requested only when you need it.
permissions.optionalIdentity: Used ONLY when you opt into automatic logging. Lets the Extension complete the Google sign-in flow that grants Gmail API access (gmail.readonly scope). Requested when you turn on automatic logging or click "Connect Gmail" in Settings > Email logging.
permissions.optionalAlarms: Used ONLY when automatic logging is active. Lets the Extension wake up periodically in the background to check for new emails on the threads you have linked. Requested when you turn on automatic logging or click "Connect Gmail".
permissions.noteDesc: The Extension only supports HTTPS connections for security. HTTP connections are not allowed.
permissions.whenRequestedIntro: Chrome will prompt you to grant optional permissions when:
permissions.whenRequested1: You configure a custom Odoo URL that is not an *.odoo.com domain
permissions.whenRequested2: You explicitly choose to connect to a self-hosted Odoo instance
permissions.canDenyDesc: if you only use Odoo Online (*.odoo.com). The Extension will work normally with Odoo Online without granting optional permissions, except automatic logging.
permissions.whyIntro: Many organizations host Odoo on their own servers with custom domains (e.g., erp.acme.com, odoo.mycompany.net). To support these users, the Extension requests optional broad permissions. However:
permissions.why1: These permissions are ONLY used to communicate with YOUR configured Odoo instance and, with automatic logging, with Google's Gmail API
permissions.why2: They are NEVER used to access other websites
permissions.why3: You can revoke them at any time in Chrome settings
permissions.why4: The Extension only requests them if you enter a custom Odoo URL or connect Gmail for automatic logging
permissions.whenRequested3: You connect Gmail for automatic logging

blogOdooGmailDomain.title: Odoo Gmail Integration: Using Your Personal Domain Without Inbox Chaos
blogOdooGmailDomain.intro: If you're an Odoo user, you've probably asked yourself: "How can I send emails from Odoo and have the customer see it's from me (name@mycompany.com) and not a generic bot?" The technical answer is straightforward, but the strategy behind it is where many companies fail. A configuration mistake can lead to privacy issues, lost emails, or an inbox where messages mysteriously appear as "read".

section1.title: Sending: Your Identity Comes First
section1.p1: For your quotes and invoices to go out with your signature and personal email, Odoo offers a robust solution: Google OAuth authentication.
section1.p2: Unlike old SMTP password configurations, OAuth lets you connect your Google Workspace account securely without sharing your actual password.
section1.howItWorksDesc: When configuring an Outgoing Mail Server with OAuth, Odoo uses a "FROM Filter". When you send an email, the system looks for a server matching your sender address.
section1.benefit1: The result: Your customer receives the email directly from you@yourcompany.com, leveraging your domain's reputation and avoiding the Spam folder.
section1.transition: So far, so good. The problem arises when we want to manage replies.

section2.title: The Trap of Personal "Incoming Servers"
section2.p1: It's tempting to think: "If I connected my outgoing, I'll connect my incoming too to have all my emails in Odoo". Be careful! This is the most common mistake.
section2.warning: Odoo's official documentation explicitly warns that the Incoming Mail Servers feature is designed for shared inboxes (like sales@ or support@), not for personal accounts.
section2.whyNotTitle: Why shouldn't you connect your personal inbox directly?
section2.problem1Desc: Odoo isn't a traditional email client. If you configure your personal account for Odoo to "pull" emails (via IMAP or POP), the system might download messages and mark them as read in your Gmail or even archive them. Imagine the frustration of opening your Gmail and not knowing what's new and what isn't.
section2.problem2Desc: In Odoo, emails attach to the Chatter (the document wall). If you sync your entire inbox, a private HR email or confidential complaint could end up visible to any colleague with system access.
section2.problem3Desc: Gmail (especially with integrated Gemini) is a superior management tool to Odoo's messaging view. By forcing work inside Odoo, you lose labels, smart filters, and Google's AI.

section3.title: The Hybrid Strategy: Centralized vs. Individual
section3.p1: The correct way to work is to divide the strategy into two flows:
section3.teamsDesc: Here we DO use full native integration. We want any email arriving at "Sales" to automatically create a CRM opportunity. It doesn't matter if it's marked as read in the original inbox, because the goal is for the team to manage it from Odoo.
section3.individualsDesc: Here we need selectivity. You want to work in your Gmail and only send to Odoo those emails relevant to the business (a negotiation, a signed invoice, etc.).

section4.title: The Solution: Connect Gmail Without Leaving Gmail
section4.p1: For personal accounts, Odoo recommends not using incoming servers, but using add-ons or extensions instead. The goal is for YOU to have control: you decide what gets saved in the CRM and what stays in your private domain.
section4.p2: Although Odoo offers a basic add-on, many users find that the workflow can be improved for those who live inside their Chrome browser and need agility.
section4.extensionTitle: Supercharge Your Workflow with Odoo Integration for Gmail
section4.extensionIntro: This is where our Chrome extension comes in, designed as a powerful alternative for demanding users. Unlike blind server synchronization, our extension allows you to:
section4.benefit1Desc: Your emails remain yours. We don't alter your inbox's "unread" status.
section4.benefit2Desc: Got an important email from a client? With a single click from your browser, send it to the corresponding record in Odoo.
section4.benefit3Desc: View Odoo data directly in your Gmail without constantly switching tabs.
section4.conclusion: Let Odoo manage company data and Gmail manage your personal communication, using our extension as the perfect bridge between both worlds.

blogApiKeySetup.title: How to Create an API Key in Odoo (All Versions)
blogApiKeySetup.intro: API keys allow external tools to connect securely to your Odoo instance without using your password. Our Gmail extension doesn't need one to connect: it uses your Odoo session. A key is an optional backup for when that session expires, and automatic logging requires one. The process to create a key varies slightly depending on your Odoo version. This guide covers every version from Odoo 14 to 19 with step-by-step instructions.

section1.title: Before You Begin
section1.p1: Before creating an API key, make sure you meet these requirements:
section1.req1: You must be logged in to your Odoo instance
section1.req2: You need an internal user account (not a portal user)
section1.req3: You should know which Odoo version you are using
section1.imgAlt: Odoo profile menu showing My Profile option
section1.tip: To check your Odoo version, look at the bottom of the Settings page or ask your system administrator.

section2.title: Odoo 14-15
section2.p1: In Odoo 14 and 15, API keys are found under the "Developer API Keys" section in your user preferences.
section2.path: Navigate to: Profile icon (top right) → My Profile → Account Security tab
section2.step2: Enter a name for your key (e.g., "Gmail Extension")
section2.step4: Copy the generated key immediately — it cannot be retrieved later
section2.warning: Odoo 15 only: If you don't see the "Developer API Keys" section, you need to activate Developer Mode first. Go to Settings → Developer Tools → Activate the developer mode, then return to your profile.
section2.note: In these versions, API keys are permanent — they never expire.

blogManageContacts.title: Managing Contacts in Odoo: The Practical Guide
blogManageContacts.intro: Duplicate records, people with no company attached, billing addresses you can't find: managing your Odoo contacts (“odoo contacts”) is often an afterthought—until it slows down your sales and skews your CRM. A clean contact database, on the other hand, saves time across the whole company.
blogManageContacts.introP2: This guide isn't about “what a contact is.” It shows, step by step, how to structure, clean and use your contacts in Odoo. Screenshots are taken on Odoo 19, but the Contacts app is stable: everything works from version 14 through 19, with a few notes where the interface differs.
blogManageContacts.introImgAlt: The contact list in the Odoo Contacts app

s1.title: Company vs individual: structuring your contacts
s1.p1: First, a fact specific to Odoo 19: the contact form no longer shows an explicit “Individual / Company” switch. That's a change from versions 14–18, where you set the type with a radio button at the top of the record. In Odoo 19, a contact created from the Contacts app is treated as a company by default—you'll see a small building icon next to the name.
s1.p2: So the hierarchy—not a toggle—is what separates companies from people. The reliable way to add a person is from their organization: open the company, go to the Contacts tab and use Add Related Contacts. Each person is then attached to their company, and you can find everyone from the company's record. You can also link an existing person to their employer through the Company field on their record.
s1.imgAltCompany: A company record in Odoo, with its linked contacts and tags
s1.p3: One company can have several addresses. When you add a child contact, Odoo offers four address types—pick the right one, because it's the one used automatically on quotations, invoices and delivery orders:
s1.addrContact: Contact: a person at the organization (sales rep, support, manager).
s1.addrInvoice: Invoice Address: where invoices are sent.
s1.addrDelivery: Delivery Address: where goods are shipped.
s1.addrOther: Other: any additional address (a secondary warehouse, etc.).
s1.imgAltAddr: Odoo dialog to create a related contact, with the Contact, Invoice, Delivery and Other types

s2.title: Managing duplicates: how to merge them
s2.p1: Duplicates are the most painful problem—and the least explained. Two records for the same customer, and your history splits in two: half the emails here, half the orders there.
s2.origin1: Leads and opportunities converted more than once.
s2.origin4: Incoming emails that create a contact automatically.
s2.howTo: The good news: Odoo ships with a merge tool. Here's how:
s2.step1: Open the Contacts app in list view.
s2.step2: Tick the contacts you want to merge (at least two).
s2.step3: Open the Actions menu and choose Merge.
s2.step4: Pick the destination contact (the one that will be kept), review the list, then click Merge Contacts.
s2.imgAltMerge: Odoo's contact merge wizard, with the destination contact selection
s2.versionNote: From version 14 to 18 the tool lives in the same place: select records in list view, then the Action(s) menu. The screen was modernized in v17-19, but the principle is identical. All linked documents (orders, invoices, emails, opportunities) are automatically reassigned to the kept contact.

s3.title: Organizing at scale: tags and categories
s3.p1: The company/person hierarchy describes structure; tags describe everything else. A single contact can carry several tags—“VIP”, “Reseller”, “Newsletter”—without touching the hierarchy.
s3.p2: You manage the tag list under Contacts ▸ Configuration ▸ Contact Tags, with a color to spot them at a glance.
s3.imgAltTags: The contact tags list in Odoo, with name, category and color
s3.p3: The point is filtering and segmenting: in list view, use Filters and Group By to isolate a tag, then save the filter as a favorite. In two clicks you get the list of all your resellers, or all customers in one region—ready to reuse for an email campaign or an export.

s4.title: Following up a contact: chatter, activities and history
s4.p1: Every record has a chatter: the thread at the bottom (or right) of the record. There you log an internal note, schedule an activity (call back, follow up) and track the full history—including the emails exchanged. It's the living “file” of the contact: everything that happened, in one place.
s4.imgAltChatter: The chatter on an Odoo contact record: messages, notes and activities
s4.mentionText: The catch: those emails live in Gmail and never reach the contact's record unless you log them by hand. You can also
s4.mentionLink: save the email to the Odoo contact's record in one click, without leaving Gmail, with our extension.

s5.title: The contact: the backbone of Odoo
s5.p1: A contact is never isolated: it's the pivot that links CRM, Sales and Invoicing. An opportunity, a quotation, an invoice, a ticket—they all point back to the same contact record.
s5.p2: Hence the simple rule: a complete, clean contact = a clean CRM. Every minute spent structuring your contacts pays off on every quote and every follow-up, because the whole chain relies on this data.

s6.title: Hygiene best practices
s6.p1: A few habits keep your database healthy over time:
s6.tip1: Fill in the email and the country: these are the key fields for deduplication and segmentation.
s6.tip2: Attach each person to their company (parent/child relationship).
s6.tip3: Use the right address type (invoice, delivery) instead of piling everything onto one record.
s6.tip4: On import, map the email column carefully and use the External ID to update existing records instead of creating new ones.
s6.tip5: Run the merge tool regularly to clear out duplicates that slipped through.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Company or individual: which should I choose in Odoo?
faq.a1: Odoo 19 no longer has an explicit Individual/Company switch on the form (it existed as a radio button in versions 14–18). In practice, model an organization as a top-level contact and a person by linking them to their company: create the company first, then add people as child contacts from the company's Contacts tab, so each person is attached to their organization.
faq.q2: How do I merge duplicate contacts in Odoo?
faq.a2: Open the Contacts app in list view, tick the contacts to merge, then open the Actions menu and choose Merge. Pick the destination contact to keep, review the list and click Merge Contacts. All linked documents are reassigned to the kept contact. The steps are the same from v14 to v19.
faq.q3: How do I save an email to a contact's record?
faq.a3: Odoo keeps emails in the record's chatter, as long as they're logged there. Inside Odoo, the chatter lets you send or log a message. To capture emails that live in Gmail, install Odoo Integration for Gmail: the extension shows the Odoo record next to your inbox and logs the email to the contact in one click, without leaving Gmail.
faq.q4: What is the difference between a contact and a lead/opportunity?
faq.a4: A contact (res.partner) is a stable record for a person or company you work with. A lead or opportunity (in CRM) is a potential deal moving through your pipeline, usually linked to a contact. One contact can generate several opportunities: the contact is the durable data, the opportunity the transient sales process.
faq.q5: How do I import contacts without creating duplicates?
faq.a5: Download Odoo's import template, map the email column correctly, and use the External ID column on re-import to update existing records instead of duplicating them. Odoo has no single anti-duplicate checkbox: after a large import, run the Merge tool from the contacts list to clean up whatever slipped through.
